PR surface: Source -25, Tests +1910, Config +2, Other +532. Total +2419 across 16 files.

target.title: fix(boundary-safety): guard response reads and UTF-16 truncation
target.body:
## Summary

- Add a boundary safety guard that inventories existing raw UTF-16 text truncation and unbounded response-body reads, then blocks newly introduced production-file violations in changed-file checks.
- Wire the guard into `pnpm check`, `pnpm check:changed`, and package scripts with a baseline so existing debt stays visible without blocking unrelated PRs.
- Fix the shared response snippet helper and representative ACP/MiniMax/provider call sites to use bounded response reads and UTF-16-safe truncation.

## Origin / follow-up

Follow-up to #97620. That PR fixed one unbounded provider response-read path. This follow-up addresses the recurring root pattern behind the recent boundary-fix cluster by adding a CI guard for new high-confidence response-body and UTF-16 text-truncation bypasses instead of continuing to rely only on one-off call-site fixes.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- #97620 is the direct source follow-up: it fixed one Google Meet Drive export bounded-read path, while this PR adds the guardrail intended to catch the same failure class when future production files change.
- #96264 is the focused MiniMax VLM success-response bound. This PR partially overlaps that call site, but it is broader: it adds the repository boundary-safety guard, baseline identity fix, JSON stdout contract, response snippet hardening, and representative bounded-read migrations.
- The MiniMax VLM success-response cap now aligns with the shared provider JSON cap at 16 MiB instead of introducing a narrower 4 MiB limit. That keeps the fail-closed behavior for oversized provider success JSON while reducing the compatibility disagreement called out by the related MiniMax-focused review path.
- If maintainers prefer #96264 as the canonical MiniMax-only route, the MiniMax hunk here can be reconciled or dropped while preserving the guard/baseline/tooling work that is unique to this PR.

## Maintainer-ready notes

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Recent boundary fixes have repeatedly patched individual channel/provider call sites for the same two failure classes: user-visible text truncated through raw UTF-16 code units, and external HTTP response bodies read without a byte cap. Without a guard, new provider/channel/plugin code can reintroduce the same failure class after the canonical helpers already exist.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause CI/tooling guard for boundary safety regressions, plus small canonical-helper hardening.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local CI/tooling enforcement path and touched helper/call-site regressions. The proof is scoped to repository guard behavior and local `Response` stream boundaries, not remote service availability.
- **Root cause:** The source invariant was missing from CI: new production code could still bypass OpenClaw's canonical UTF-16 and bounded-response helpers even though those helpers existed. A few shared helpers and representative call sites also still contained raw response reads or raw head truncation, so the repository had no enforced contract that new boundary code must use the canonical owners.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This root-cause fix enforces the missing repository invariant at the source: new production code must not introduce high-confidence raw UTF-16 head truncation or unbounded awaited `Response` body reads. `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` scans production TypeScript with the TypeScript AST, compares findings to a checked-in baseline, and fails only on new changed-file violations. It catches high-confidence raw string head truncation and awaited external `Response` body reads while avoiding tests, fixtures, generated/vendor code, Express response writers, hash/protocol slices, and collection slicing. Baseline identity is stable across line-only movement by comparing file/rule/match counts instead of treating line numbers as part of the violation identity. `scripts/check-changed.mjs` runs the guard for core/extension changes, while `scripts/check.mjs` checks full baseline drift.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not rewrite all legacy baseline entries, add new public APIs, change response-size defaults outside the touched MiniMax success path, or modify credentials/configuration. Full legacy remediation and exhaustive taint analysis are out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` is the source-of-truth validator for new boundary-safety violations; `test/fixtures/boundary-safety-inventory.json` is the baseline contract for current legacy inventory; `src/infra/http-body.ts` is the canonical bounded response/snippet helper for core runtime code; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` exposes the bounded response reader to plugin code; `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` remains the canonical UTF-16-safe truncation owner.
- **Patch quality notes:** The guard is intentionally high-confidence rather than exhaustive: it prevents new clear bypasses without forcing noisy legacy cleanup. After sync with current `origin/main`, the baseline contains 232 known entries; the earlier branch baseline dropped entries already fixed upstream and absorbed current main inventory drift. Related open PR scan found no open PR already adding these guard rule names.
- **Target test file:** `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts`, `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts`, `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts`, `src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts`, and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** New raw `messageText.slice(0, maxChars - 1)` text truncation is flagged; `truncateUtf16Safe(...)` is accepted; collection/hash/protocol slices are ignored; awaited `response.json()` / `res.text().catch(...)` reads are flagged; Express `res.json({...})` writers are ignored; a baseline-known finding remains accepted when only its line number moves; `--json` mode keeps stdout parseable while routing human status text to stderr; diagnostic snippets cancel exact-cap stalling streams; MiniMax tests now exercise real `Response` bodies for bounded JSON reads and prove a 5 MiB success JSON succeeds under the shared 16 MiB cap while a body over 16 MiB is canceled and rejected.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The guard uses a baseline plus changed-file enforcement instead of a broad rewrite, so the test guardrail proves the invariant for new code while leaving legacy entries visible but non-blocking. It intentionally covers only high-confidence AST patterns and explains patch quality warnings from default returns/catches as fail-closed parser branches, not runtime fallbacks that mask user behavior.

## Root Cause

The root cause is a missing repository-level source invariant for boundary code. User-visible text can still be shortened with raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing, which can leave dangling surrogate halves when the cut lands inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character. Remote HTTP responses can still be read with `response.json()`, `response.text()`, or `response.arrayBuffer()` directly, which buffers the entire body before OpenClaw can enforce the intended byte budget.

The canonical helpers existed, but the repository did not have a changed-file guard that forced new production code toward those helpers. As a result, each fix landed as a local call-site patch, while the next integration change could reintroduce the same boundary bypass in a sibling area. The shared response snippet path also still carried a raw no-stream fallback and raw character slicing, so even helper consumers were not fully protected.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** New production code that bypasses UTF-16-safe text truncation or bounded response-body helpers is now caught by the changed-file guard, while existing legacy findings remain tracked in a full-repo baseline. MiniMax VLM success JSON now uses the same bounded provider JSON reader with a 16 MiB cap, preserving normal provider-sized success responses while rejecting/canceling oversized bodies. After the conflict sync, the shared snippet path also cancels exact-cap diagnostic reads and no longer falls back to an unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` path when no readable stream is available.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw repair worktree at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774`, branch `repair/pr-97774`, after syncing PR #97774 onto current `origin/main`. The exercised behavior is repository CI/tooling enforcement plus local `Response` stream boundary handling.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && pnpm check:boundary-safety
```


```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && node scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --json > /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-97774-evidence/boundary-json-stdout-after-sync.json 2> /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-97774-evidence/boundary-json-stderr-after-sync.txt
```

```bash
node -e "const fs=require('node:fs'); const dir='/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-97774-evidence'; const stdout=fs.readFileSync(dir + '/boundary-json-stdout-after-sync.json','utf8'); const stderr=fs.readFileSync(dir + '/boundary-json-stderr-after-sync.txt','utf8'); const parsed=JSON.parse(stdout); if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) throw new Error('stdout was not a JSON array'); if (stdout.includes('Boundary safety changed-file check passed')) throw new Error('stdout contained human status text'); if (!stderr.includes('Boundary safety changed-file check passed')) throw new Error('stderr did not contain human status text'); console.log('JSON stdout parse check passed; entries=' + parsed.length);"
```



```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts
```

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts
```

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts
```

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts
```

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.media-understanding.config.ts src/media-understanding/image.test.ts
```

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && pnpm tsgo:core
```

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 && pnpm lint:scripts
```

```bash
git -C /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774 diff --check
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

Boundary safety changed-file check passed (0 changed-file entries, all baseline-known).
$ node scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --all

JSON stdout parse check passed; entries=0
```




```text
Tests  29 passed (29)

```


```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

```text
pnpm tsgo:core completed without diagnostics.
pnpm lint:scripts completed the docker-e2e, raw-http2, and scripts oxlint checks.
git diff --check exited 0 with no whitespace errors.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The full guard baseline matches 232 known legacy entries on the synced repair worktree, while the changed-file guard passes because the patch itself introduces no new unbaseline-known violations. `node scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --json` leaves stdout parseable as a JSON array and writes the human success status to stderr. `pnpm check:changed --dry-run` includes `pnpm check:boundary-safety`, proving the guard is wired into the changed-file path. The focused test suite verifies UTF-16-safe snippet/progress truncation, bounded response reads, JSON stdout behavior, line-shift-stable baseline identity, MiniMax success JSON acceptance below 16 MiB, MiniMax oversized-body cancellation above 16 MiB, and exact-cap diagnostic snippet cancellation.
- **What was not tested:** No browser UI, hosted CI run, or remote MiniMax availability is claimed. Remote MiniMax is not required to prove this patch because the changed behavior is the local fetch/`Response` body boundary, which is exercised with real `Response` streams. `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and `pnpm lint:core` were not rerun for this conflict-only update.

## Review findings addressed

- **Proof request / real behavior evidence:** The reviewer-facing proof is mapped to the actual behavior changed here: repository guard execution, baseline diffing, and local `Response` stream boundary handling. No browser UI, hosted CI rerun, or remote MiniMax availability is claimed.
- **RF-001 — automation gate risk:** Verified against current main after the conflict sync: changed-file enforcement passes with 0 new entries, full baseline matches 232 entries, and `pnpm check:changed --dry-run` shows the guard is wired into the changed-file path. The remaining question is maintainer acceptance of the guard policy, not an unresolved merge conflict.
- **RF-002 — MiniMax success-response compatibility:** The MiniMax success path remains aligned to the shared 16 MiB provider JSON cap. The compatibility tradeoff for responses above 16 MiB is documented as fail-closed behavior and locked by `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts`.
- **RF-003 — body-less HTTP error snippet overlap:** The conflict sync keeps the shared snippet helper bounded: standard readable `Response` streams are prefix-read and exact-cap diagnostic streams are canceled; non-readable/no-stream responses return no snippet rather than using an unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` fallback. If maintainers prefer byte-clamped non-stream diagnostics from the sibling path, that is a policy choice outside this conflict repair.
- **RF-004 — maintainer policy boundary:** The remaining automation/compatibility questions are explicitly documented in the merge-risk section. This update resolves the merge conflict and current-head local verification without broadening scope into a new guard policy redesign.

## CI follow-up addressed

- **Current-head CI attribution:** The earlier compact-check failures on the previous head were current-PR direct regressions, not stale/main-baseline/infra failures. `checks-node-compact-small-whole-1` failed MiniMax/image-tool tests plus an exact-cap PDF error-body test; `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` failed MiniMax media-understanding tests. Both failure classes line up with this PR's bounded MiniMax JSON reader and response-snippet boundary changes.
- **Fix applied:** MiniMax test fixtures now return real JSON `Response` bodies, with fresh bodies for multi-image calls, so the tests exercise the same bounded `Response.body` path as production. Diagnostic text snippets cancel exact-cap stalling streams, while `readResponseWithLimit` keeps its success-response overflow semantics. The conflict sync also keeps `src/infra/http-body.ts` free of the unbounded no-stream `arrayBuffer()` fallback flagged by the new guard.
- **Latest focused verification:** After syncing onto current `origin/main`, reran the guard checks, JSON stdout parse check, changed-check dry-run, boundary-safety tests, infra response-body tests, MiniMax boundary tests, ACP manager tests, image-tool tests, PDF provider tests, media-understanding image tests, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm lint:scripts`, and `git diff --check`.

## Regression Test Plan

- `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts` locks guard detection and false-positive boundaries for string truncation, response-body reads, Express writers, collection slices, baseline diffing, line-shift-stable baseline identity, and parseable `--json` stdout.
- `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts` locks bounded response snippet behavior, UTF-16-safe snippet truncation, and exact-cap diagnostic stream cancellation.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts` locks success-response acceptance below the shared 16 MiB cap and overflow cancellation above the cap.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` lock MiniMax callers against real bounded JSON `Response` bodies instead of `.json()`-only mocks.
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts` locks exact-cap provider error-body cancellation.
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts` locks parented ACP task progress truncation without dangling surrogate halves.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** CI/tooling, boundary safety, provider response reads, UTF-16 text truncation, provider compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The guard can block new changed-file code that uses raw response reads or raw string truncation in production files. It should not block unrelated legacy debt because existing entries are baseline-known by stable file/rule/match identity, not by fragile line numbers, and it intentionally excludes tests/fixtures/generated/vendor files plus common false positives. MiniMax VLM success responses over 16 MiB now fail closed through the bounded provider JSON reader instead of fully buffering the body.
- **Why acceptable:** The failure mode is actionable: use `truncateUtf16Safe`, `sliceUtf16Safe`, `readResponseWithLimit`, `readResponseTextSnippet`, `readProviderJsonResponse`, or add a narrow `boundary-safety-ignore <rule-id>: <reason>` for a proven false positive. This turns a repeated review/bug pattern into a local CI failure before PR submission. The MiniMax cap now matches the shared provider JSON response cap, so normal provider-sized success JSON has the same budget as other bounded provider JSON paths.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** This PR does not attempt full legacy remediation, exhaustive taint analysis, or live third-party provider/channel validation.
